_🩺 Stability & Availability_ | _🟠 Major_ | _🏗️ Heavy lift_

**Add a timeout to the writer-gate wait so a second begin on the same thread cannot hang forever.**

`TransactionWriters` holds one process-wide `SemaphoreSlim(1, 1)` for each mutex name. The holder thread keeps the permit until `Run` reaches its `finally` block at line 120. That happens only after the first handle completes.

`gate.Wait(closing)` waits with no timeout. Consider one thread that calls `db.BeginTransaction()` twice without completing the first handle. The second call blocks forever, because only that same thread can complete the first handle. The same hang occurs with a second `LiteDatabase` instance in the same process if the first handle is never completed. The only exit is a close from another thread, which cancels `closing`.

The legacy Shared path and the Direct handle path report lock waits through the engine timeout. This gate ignores `_settings.Timeout`.

Use a bounded wait and throw the existing LiteDB lock-timeout exception when the wait expires.

<details>
<summary>🐛 Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
             var gate = TransactionWriters.GetOrAdd(name, _ => new SemaphoreSlim(1, 1));
             // Pending begins use their caller's synchronous wait, never a holder thread/engine.
-            gate.Wait(closing);
+            if (!gate.Wait(_settings.Timeout, closing))
+                throw LiteException.LockTimeout("transaction", _settings.Timeout);
```
</details>

Confirm the name of the `EngineSettings` timeout property and the lock-timeout factory that this codebase uses.

_📐 Maintainability & Code Quality_ | _🟡 Minor_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Keep the holder thread's stack trace when you rethrow `_error`.**

`_error` is captured on the holder thread. `Release()` rethrows it with `throw _error`, which replaces the original stack trace from `OpenDatabase` or cleanup. Line 84 also has an unreachable `throw _error;`, because `Release()` has already thrown whenever `_error` is set. As a result, a failed Shared handle open shows only the stack of `Release`.

<details>
<summary>🩹 Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-                if (_error != null) { Release(); throw _error; }
+                if (_error != null) Release();
```

```diff
-                if (_error != null) throw _error;
+                if (_error != null) System.Runtime.ExceptionServices.ExceptionDispatchInfo.Capture(_error).Throw();
```
</details>





Also applies to: 132-132

The wait is intentional in this slice and follows the existing Shared native-admission contract; `EngineSettings` has no `Timeout` property. The persisted TIMEOUT pragma governs collection/engine locks, while `SharedEngine.EnterOwner` and the legacy native owner also wait until release. Reading that pragma to obtain a timeout here would itself require the native ownership being awaited. The revised #3064/#3067 contracts explicitly allow backend admission to block. The new gate remains cancellable by session close, with regressions for queued begins and native contention. I expanded docs/transaction-handles.md to state the same-caller second-begin hazard explicitly. A new Shared admission deadline would need a separately defined setting and coverage across the local gate and native wait; applying a timeout only to this gate would give inconsistent cross-process behavior.

Fixed in cf7362a1f: Release now rethrows the holder error through ExceptionDispatchInfo, and Open no longer contains the unreachable second throw. The focused 96-case handle/completion run passes, including failed-open and cleanup paths.

`@JKamsker`, thanks for fixing both points in `cf7362a1f`. The `ExceptionDispatchInfo` rethrow preserves the holder thread’s stack trace, and removing the second throw removes unreachable code. Thanks for reporting the 96-case test results.

`@JKamsker`, thanks for the clarification. I withdraw this finding.

My proposed fix incorrectly assumed that `EngineSettings.Timeout` exists. It also treated the persisted `TIMEOUT` pragma as an admission deadline.

Under the stated contract, `gate.Wait(closing)` is intentional. The same-caller second-begin hazard does not justify a gate-only timeout. A Shared admission deadline would need a separate setting and consistent behavior across both the local gate and native admission.
